evidence_private: INT4B16/P25-PARITY.md (P27 phases 4, 7, 7b, 8)
claims.notes: Cache flag is a bit-exact no-op (cached prefill == short forward). Real vs random continuation moves prefix positions 0.24% at layer 1 -> 34% at layer 19 (bf16 batch-shape variance in the expert gathers, amplified by the router); Qwen3-30B: 0.15% -> 3.5%, NLL 0.001. Running the router in fp32 (plain transformers) does not remove the amplification (layer-19 divergence 0.25 against 0.34, top layer unchanged) and itself moves the same tokens' NLL by 1.1 nats, so router precision is not a lever; the sensitivity is the model's.

claims.notes: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-04, number unchanged. The measurement stands exactly as its receipt made it (docs/METHODOLOGY.md section 10; bench/_upstream/bench_energy.py, bench/bench_energy_excluded.py). What is withdrawn is the parenthetical mechanism 'NF4 is storage-only, the GEMM runs in bf16 either way', which was a universal present-tense statement about every bitsandbytes 4-bit path: it is true of the two 4-bit arms this receipt measured (dequantize-then-linear, and the bitsandbytes#1965 fork's matmul_4bit routing on a [packed, 1] weight, on one Ampere card) and of this package's own reference training path, but bitsandbytes >= 0.50.0 CUDA inference can consume packed 4-bit weights directly for supported ordinary 2-D cells (docs/BITSANDBYTES.md), routed grouped MoE execution is a separate contract, and training's input gradient is separate again. The receipt identifies the bitsandbytes build only as '0.50.0.dev0' / 'the fork (bnb 0.50-dev)' (METHODOLOGY section 1 and its packaging note) -- no commit SHA, and the harness does not print bitsandbytes.__version__ -- so whether that build carried upstream 5453368bed15d19cbcfba4426ed118de33dc3d94 is not recoverable from it; the remeasure with a recorded version is e4b#392. Successor: e4b.train.energy-honest.scoped-a2000 (same value, comparator and version scoped).

claims.claim: On a card that already fits the model, 4-bit expert projections cost 1.2-2.3x the GPU energy of native bf16 on the measured comparator: one OLMoE-dims gate_up projection (NF4 through Experts4bit) on an RTX A2000, bitsandbytes 0.50.0.dev0 (the bitsandbytes#1965 fork build; exact commit unrecorded), measured as dequantize-then-linear and the fork's matmul_4bit routing on a [packed, 1] weight against F.linear on the bf16 weight, at decode M=1 and prefill M=512 (no grad) and train fwd+bwd M=32 (grad enabled). It inverts when memory binds: on the same card bf16 OLMoE-1B-7B does not fit at all, and the fused 4-bit MoE forward's freed memory unlocks a batch worth up to 4.4x lower energy per token (64 -> 4096 tokens).
claims.unit: x GPU energy per op vs native bf16, model already fits (one-projection microbench)

claims.claim: OPEN: no shipped tool bakes the arena.
